scores.reason: Directly tests the brief's premise: shows search effort and accuracy are weakly aligned, ties accuracy to cumulative retrieval recall, and isolates redundant reformulation — hits C2 and C5 and informs decisions 2 and 4.
Fixed-corpus benchmark with human-verified labels that separates retriever from agent and reports BM25/embedding baselines — the anchor for decision 1 (C1) and a model case for decision 3 (C4).

The clearest gain-non-replication evidence in the list: evidence recall collapses from 84.3% to 21.4% when the corpus is no longer curated per query — squarely C4 and C5, the work the brief says to reach hardest for.

Trajectory-level evidence that iterative crawling by itself carries little gain, with a quantified controller intervention isolating what does — directly answers decision 2 (C2) and undercuts the premise (C5-adjacent).
Survey/taxonomy of DR agent designs plus a critique of benchmark limitations; useful framing for decisions 2 and 3 but contributes no measurement of its own.

An actual scientific-literature system combining hybrid retrieval, knowledge-graph traversal and agentic self-correction (C3), though its evaluation measures extraction quality rather than search recall, so it informs the design decisions only partially.

A second independently constructed DR benchmark with expert-crafted references and citation-accuracy metrics — real material for decision 3 (C4), though it evaluates report quality more than retrieval recall.

Inertia bias is an interesting agent-judgment failure mode, but it bears on answer validation, not on retrieval recall ceilings, mechanism-attributed gains, benchmark construction, or gain replication — shares the domain without answering any of the brief's four questions.

Quantified isolation of reformulation-plus-graph-traversal gains (C2/C3), but demonstrated on generic multi-hop QA over Wikipedia entity graphs, not citation graphs or literature search — relevant mechanism evidence with an acknowledged transfer gap.

Detailed, labor-intensive benchmark-construction precedent (C4) showing fine-grained rubric labeling exposes gaps coarser metrics hide — informs decision 3, though its focus is report quality rather than literature retrieval.
